title: Algebraic Attacks on Non-Polynomial Ciphers over Integer Rings
summary: Algebraic attacks require polynomial representations, but their threat to integer-ring ciphers lacking one remains uncharacterized.

formal_statement.body: Algebraic attacks, including interpolation, higher-order differential, and Gr?bner-basis attacks, require a polynomial representation to work. Characterize whether and to what extent this class of attacks can threaten ciphers over the integer ring $\mathbb{Z}_{p^n}$ when those ciphers do not admit a polynomial representation.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of symmetric ciphers over integer rings without polynomial representations.
parameters: p^n, the modulus defining the integer ring
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize whether and to what extent algebraic attacks can threaten ciphers over the integer ring with modulus p^n that do not admit a polynomial representation.

citations.label: The ABC of Symmetric Primitives over Integer Rings: Milk Before Meat

progress.summary: The source presents polynomial representation as a requirement for the named algebraic attacks, then identifies the threat to integer-ring ciphers without such a representation as unclear at the current state of the art.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., The ABC of Symmetric Primitives over Integer Rings: Milk Before Meat
